warnings: Copper is tracked as a target with a ceiling: 1.7 mg/day goal (ICMR-NIN via FSSAI, secondary, unverified); upper limit 10 mg/day (US), 5 mg/day (EFSA).
Never suggest a copper supplement to fill the ring; food provides enough for almost everyone.
Wilson disease and Menkes disease are doctor-led (requires_doctor_input): no targets, no diet rules, show 'Follow your doctor's advice'.
Zinc supplements of 25 mg or more daily for more than 4 weeks can lower copper; suggest asking a doctor or pharmacist.
Anaemia that does not respond to iron, numbness or unsteady walking (especially after weight-loss surgery or long zinc use): talk to your doctor.
Do not boil or store milk (especially infant milk) in brass or copper vessels; avoid unlined copper or brass for acidic food such as tamarind, curd, tomato or lemon dishes.
Water stored in copper vessels gains copper with time (up to 0.82 mg/L in 168 hours in one Indian test); not advised for children, liver disease or Wilson disease.
Liver (organ meat) is the only common food that can overshoot the daily target in one serving; keep portions small.
Do not use IFCT octopus (R003 6.72 mg/100 g), beef liver (O032) or calf liver (O042): suspect values.
